about: spec-v1974: per-state adoption of the IBC, drafted one state at a time from the state's own statute or rule, with ICC's adoption chart (April 2026) as the cross-check only. All 51 drafted 2026-10-20; unsigned rows show labeled not verified, and a row whose sources conflict shows no edition.

AL.name: Alabama
AL.scope: State code covers state-owned or state-funded work, K-12 and public postsecondary schools, hotels/motels and movie theaters only.
AL.citation: Ala. Admin. Code r. 355-12-1-.01 (Alabama State Building Code: 2021 IBC with 2024 IBC sections), DCM
AL.draft_note: Read rule 355-12-1-.01 PDF: 'The minimum building standard code adopted by the Division of Construction Management is the 2021 International Building Code', with Ch.2 flammable-gas definition and Table 307.1(1), 307.4, 307.5, 414.2.5, Table 414.5.1 replaced by 2024 IBC sections (refrigerant changes per Act 2023-276). Rule history: amended eff 2022-04-14 (2021 adoption) and eff 2025-03-17 (2024 sections). Read DCM State Building Code page: '2021 International Building Code adopted on July 1, 2022'; jurisdiction limited to state property/state funds, schools, hotels/motels, movie theaters; DCM has no jurisdiction over other commercial or residential property. A 2022 DCM bulletin (search summary only) says submittals on/after 2023-01-01 must comply. Effective date choice: 2022-07-01 (DCM page) vs rule eff 2022-04-14; signer pick. Other commercial buildings: local adoption.
AL.icc_2026_10_20: Chart: IBC 21. State page: Building Commission adopts codes for state funded buildings, hotels, motels, movie theaters, and schools; links dcm.alabama.gov.

AK.name: Alaska
AK.pending: DPS review of the 2024 IBC/IEBC/IFC/IMC/IFGC underway; public notice estimated summer 2026, none found.
AK.scope: Applies to all occupancies except 1-3 family dwellings and small townhouses; deferred cities and boroughs enforce it locally.
AK.citation: 13 AAC 50.020 (2021 IBC as amended), Alaska State Fire Marshal, Dept. of Public Safety
AK.draft_note: Read 13 AAC 50.020 on akleg.gov (print view): 'The International Building Code 2021 Edition (IBC), Chapters 1 - 12, 14 - 28, and 30 - 35, and Appendix C are adopted by reference to regulate all occupancies and buildings', with Alaska revisions; 101.2 exceptions: detached 1-, 2-, 3-family dwellings and townhouses <=3 stories. The print view omits the history line, so the effective date 2022-10-28 comes from the Mat-Su Borough page ('takes effect on October 28, 2022') and a search summary of the DPS regulations page (DPS page returned 404). A July 2026 DPS document (search summary only) says the 2024 codes review is underway with public notice estimated summer 2026; no notice found. Signer: confirm the Register effective date.
AK.icc_2026_10_20: Chart: IBC 21. State page: codes are mandatory under state inspection unless a local jurisdiction is a 'deferred jurisdiction'; Alaska amendments to IBC/IEBC/IFC/IMC/IFGC 2021.

AZ.name: Arizona
AZ.scope: No statewide building code; cities and counties adopt their own edition. The State Fire Code (2018 IFC) covers state buildings and schools.
AZ.citation: No state adoption: counties adopt building codes under A.R.S. 11-861; cities by reference under A.R.S. 9-802
AZ.draft_note: An absence has no adopting rule to cite. Read A.R.S. 11-861 (zoned counties may adopt a building code for unincorporated areas, may exempt rural zones) and 9-802 (municipal adoption by reference) on azleg.gov. No state IBC adoption found. ICC says the State Fire Marshal reviews plans for state/county buildings and schools, and all non-small-residential construction where no local fire code, under the 2018 IFC (a fire code, not the IBC). citation_primary true because the statutes read show local authority; signer may prefer false as for other absences.
AZ.icc_2026_10_20: Chart: IBC X. State page: 'Codes are adopted locally in Arizona and are predominantly the I-codes'; State Fire Code adopts the 2018 IFC.

AR.name: Arkansas
AR.citation: Ark. Code R. 015.01.22-005, 2021 Arkansas Fire Prevention Code, Volume II (Building), State Fire Marshal
AR.draft_note: Read the rule text (Cornell LII copy): the 2021 IFC, IBC and IRC as amended by the State Fire Marshal 'shall constitute the Arkansas Fire Prevention Code, 2021 Edition. These Rules shall be effective January 1,2023'; 'INTERNATIONAL BUILDING CODE shall mean the Arkansas Fire Prevention Code, Volume II'. Search summaries: localities may adopt and enforce only the AFPC 2021; Oct 2024 DPS foreword revisions still say 2021. No 2024-edition rulemaking found. Building code sits within the state fire code; enforcement is local or by the fire marshal.
AR.icc_2026_10_20: Chart: IBC 21. State page: State Fire Marshal's office, Dept. of Health and Energy Office adopt Arkansas' codes.

CA.name: California
CA.citation: Cal. Code Regs. tit. 24, pt. 2 (2025 California Building Code), Building Standards Commission
CA.draft_note: Read DGS/BSC codes page: 2025 Title 24 'published July 1, 2025, with an effective date of January 1, 2026'; Part 2 (CBC Vols 1 & 2) errata effective 2026-01-01. Prior 2022 CBC (2021 IBC) eff 2023-01-01. The 2024 IBC base comes from the SFM rulemaking draft ('2024 International Building Code ... with necessary California amendments') and the ICC product listing, not the BSC page. Cities and counties may adopt more restrictive local amendments filed with BSC; state agencies (DSA, HCAI, SFM) enforce for schools, hospitals and state buildings.
CA.icc_2026_10_20: Chart: IBC 24. State page: 'The 2025 California Codes are available!'; adopted at state level, enforced locally except public schools and hospitals.

CO.name: Colorado
CO.scope: No statewide code; state rules cover only buildings under DFPC (public schools, health facilities) and state-owned buildings.
CO.citation: 8 CCR 1507-101, rule 3.2.1 (2021 IBC), Division of Fire Prevention and Control
CO.draft_note: Read 8 CCR 1507-101 art. 3 (Cornell LII): 3.2.1 adopts 'International Building Code- 2021 Edition' for property subject to DFPC oversight (C.R.S. 44-30-515, 24-33.5 Part 12); rule notes: rules 3.1, 3.2 eff 06/30/2021; 3.1 says new work after July 1, 2021 meets new-construction rules. Read DFPC FLS Adopted Codes page: same list; 'projects submitted for plan review prior to 1 July, 2021 will be reviewed under the previously adopted Codes'. A CU facilities doc says 2021 IBC effective July 1, 2022 (not state rule). Separately the Office of the State Architect adopts the 2021 IBC for state agency and higher-ed buildings (search summary of OSA exhibit rev. 8/2023; PDF blocked), and the Division of Housing enforces codes for hotels/motels/multifamily where no local code (not checked). All other buildings: local adoption.
CO.icc_2026_10_20: Chart: IBC X. State page: 'Colorado has no statewide building code'; State Buildings Program sets codes for state construction; DFPC adopts codes for public K-12 schools and health facilities.

CT.name: Connecticut
CT.pending: 2026 State Building Code (2024 IBC) awaits Legislative Regulation Review Committee approval; July 1, 2026 date delayed, no new date.
CT.citation: 2022 Connecticut State Building Code (2021 IBC as amended), Office of the State Building Inspector, C.G.S. 29-252
CT.draft_note: Read DAS regulations page: 'The 2022 Connecticut State Building Code applies to projects with permit applications filed from October 1, 2022' and adopts the 2021 IBC. Read DAS adoption-process page: next codes 'were expected to take effect on July 1, 2026, but ... we await approval ... by the Legislative Regulation Review Committee ... the effective date has been delayed'. Search: LRRC rejected without prejudice 2025-12-16; resubmitted (LCO memo 2026-04-28). Codes cannot be amended locally. Statute section not checked; signer confirm C.G.S. cite.
CT.icc_2026_10_20: Chart: IBC 21. State page: based on the 2021 International Codes; 2022 CSBC applies to permit applications filed from October 1, 2022; cannot be amended locally.

DE.name: Delaware
DE.scope: No statewide building code; the three counties and municipalities adopt their own edition.
DE.citation: No state adoption: 16 Del. C. 7601 lets the three counties adopt and enforce building codes
DE.draft_note: Read 16 Del. C. ch. 76: 7601 the Kent Levy Court and New Castle/Sussex County Councils 'may adopt and enforce building codes'; 7602 sets a state minimum energy code only. No statewide IBC adoption found. citation_primary true because the statute read shows local authority; signer may prefer false. County editions not checked.
DE.icc_2026_10_20: Chart: IBC X. State page: 'Building Codes are adopted at the county and municipal level'; statewide adoption only for the IPC and IECC.

FL.name: Florida
FL.pending: 9th Edition (2026) Florida Building Code proposed 2026-09-23 (comment period closed 2026-10-14); no final notice or date yet.
FL.citation: Fla. Admin. Code r. 61G20-1.001 (Florida Building Code, 8th Edition (2023), Building), Florida Building Commission
FL.draft_note: Read flrules page for 61G20-1.001: latest final version eff 2026-03-18; history includes amended 12-31-23 (8th Edition (2023) adoption; later amendments 2024-2026 are statutory updates). Read the 2026-09-23 proposed notice: adopts the 9th Edition (2026) as the s. 553.73(7)(a) triennial update; states no effective date or base I-code edition. Listed as pending, not upcoming. ICC/Miami-Dade (from IRC drafting) say 9th Ed effective 2026-12-31; recheck in Dec 2026. The 2021 IBC base of the 8th Edition is from ICC/secondary sources, not the rule page.
FL.icc_2026_10_20: Chart: IBC 21. State page: Florida Building Code 8th Edition (2023) with Commission-approved supplements.

GA.name: Georgia
GA.scope: Mandatory state minimum code; local governments choose whether to enforce, and local amendments must be filed with DCA.
GA.citation: O.C.G.A. 8-2-23; DCA State Minimum Standard Codes: 2024 IBC with Georgia Amendments
GA.draft_note: Read DCA memo dated 2025-12-01: the DCA Board 'voted to adopt the following codes with an effective date of January 1, 2026', including the '2024 International Building Code with Georgia Amendments', as mandatory state codes under O.C.G.A. 8-2-23. Prior edition (2018 IBC) not recorded here.
GA.icc_2026_10_20: Chart: IBC 24. State page: adopted at state level by DCA; enforcement left to local AHJ; local codes must be the same as the state's; IBC adopted with Georgia Amendments.

HI.name: Hawaii
HI.pending: SBCC 2021-code work suspended under the Governor's housing proclamation; 2021 IBC said to apply by default without amendments.
HI.scope: State code becomes each county's interim code if the county does not adopt it within 2 years; counties amend and enforce.
HI.citation: Haw. Admin. R. tit. 3, State Building Code Council definitions: State Building Code (2018 IBC) [Eff 4/20/2021]; HRS ch. 107
HI.draft_note: SOURCES CONFLICT: HAR definitions (Cornell LII) say 'IBC' means the State Building Code 'adopting and amending the International Building Code, 2018 Edition' [Eff 4/20/2021], and Honolulu's 2024 ordinance adopts the state code 'as adopted by the State of Hawaii on April 20, 2021' (2018 IBC); ICC chart also says 18. But the SBCC Annual Report (read during IRC drafting) says the 2021 IBC, IRC and IECC 'were adopted by default in the State without state amendments' (HRS 107: a national code becomes the state code if not adopted in 2 years). Which edition a permit uses depends on the county ordinance. Signer: decide 2018 vs 2021 default.
HI.icc_2026_10_20: Chart: IBC 18. State page: core codes based on IBC, IRC, IECC, UPC; counties have 2 years to amend, else the State Code becomes the county's code.

ID.name: Idaho
ID.pending: Building Code Board proposed the 2024 IBC (minutes 2025-08-11); the June 2026 rule text still adopts the 2018 IBC.
ID.scope: Applied by cities and counties that run a permit program (Idaho Code 39-4116) and by the Division for public buildings and schools.
ID.citation: IDAPA 24.39.30.600.01 (Idaho Building Code Board; International Building Code, 2018 Edition, amended)
ID.draft_note: Read the current IDAPA 24.39.30 PDF (created 2026-06-12): 600.01 adopts the 2018 IBC with accessibility appendices and Idaho amendments (day care/custodial care R-3, fixture footnotes, deletes 3113); 600.02 adds the 2021 IBC mass-timber (IV-A/B/C) provisions. Stamped (7-1-24). Read Idaho Code 39-4109: codes are adopted for the Division and 'shall only be applied by local governments as prescribed by section 39-4116'; 39-4109(4) and the 2020 rule say a new edition takes effect January 1 after adoption/legislative approval. The 2020 temporary rule (3-20-20)T adopted the 2018 IBC, so 2021-01-01 is the effective date (matches the IRC row; optional early use from 2020-07-01 per secondary sources). Read 39-4116: localities with permit programs must adopt the IBC by Jan 1 after Board adoption, may amend to an equal level of protection, and 1-2 family sprinkler mandates are exempted. 'limited' because nothing I read applies the IBC where no local program exists, apart from Division jurisdiction over public buildings and school facilities. Board minutes (2025-08-11) list a proposed 2024 IBC adoption (with removal of the 2021 mass-timber carve-out); no final rule seen.

IL.name: Illinois
IL.scope: No statewide building code; cities and counties adopt their own. Elsewhere, commercial buildings are inspected to the current or prior IBC.
IL.citation: 20 ILCS 3105/10.09-1 and 10.18 (Capital Development Board Act, as amended by P.A. 103-510, eff. 2024-01-01)
IL.draft_note: Read P.A. 103-510 on ilga.gov. 20 ILCS 3105/10.09-1: no one may occupy a new or substantially improved commercial building in a 'non-building code jurisdiction' until a qualified inspector certifies compliance with 'the current edition or most recent preceding edition' of the IBC (incl. Appendix G, excl. ch. 11, 13, 29) and the IEBC, plus the NEC, the state energy/stretch code, Illinois Accessibility Code and Illinois Plumbing Code. So in such areas the 2024 or 2021 IBC applies via inspection; there is no single edition. 10.18(e): from 2025-01-01 any municipal or county building code must be at least as stringent in structural design as the 'baseline building code' (the least restrictive IBC edition published in the current or preceding 9 years). State-owned construction: AWC (secondary) lists the 2021 IBC for the Capital Development Board; I did not read a CDB rule or manual naming it. 'local' with editions [] per the brief; signer may consider 'limited'.
IL.icc_2026_10_20: Master I-Code chart (April 2026): IBC X (local adoptions only).

IN.name: Indiana
IN.pending: 2026 Indiana Building Code (2024 IBC, new 675 IAC 13-2.7) drafted by the FPBSC; LSA number and effective date not yet set.
IN.citation: 675 IAC 13-2.6 (2014 Indiana Building Code, based on the 2012 IBC)
IN.draft_note: Read the Indiana Department of Homeland Security FPBSC rules page: 675 IAC 13-2.6, 2014 Indiana Building Code, adopts the IBC 2012 Edition, First Printing, and ANSI A117.1-2009, 'Currently in Effect, Effective: 12/1/2014'. I did not read the IAC text itself (Justia 403). Also read the IDHS 'Building Code LSA Document 6.1.2026' draft: adds 675 IAC 13-2.7 adopting the 2024 IBC (first printing August 2023) as the 2026 Indiana Building Code and repeals 13-2.6; LSA # is 'XX-XXX' and 'Effective XXXX'. The regulatory analysis says the anticipated effective date is 'To Be Determined'. Indiana rules apply statewide; localities may adopt only Commission-approved local amendments (not re-read here).

IA.name: Iowa
IA.scope: State code applies to state-owned or state-funded buildings, localities that accept it, and cities over 15,000 with no local code.
IA.citation: 481 IAC 301.3(103A) (State Building Code; International Building Code, 2024 edition, amended)
IA.draft_note: Read 481 IAC ch. 301 (IAC 9/30/26). Rule 301.3 adopts the 2024 IBC by reference with amendments (deletes most of ch. 1, ch. 29 and most appendices; retains App. C) [ARC 9474C, IAB 8/6/25, eff. 9/10/25]. Rules moved from 661 to 481 on 11/26/25; old 661-301 copies are out of date. Rule 301.10: projects commenced within 12 months of the effective date (to about 2026-09-10) could use the prior standards. Read Iowa Code 103A.10(2): the state code applies to state-owned buildings, subdivisions that accept it by ordinance, state-funded new construction, and cities over 15,000 without a local code substantially per a national model code; energy provisions apply statewide. Hence 'limited'.

KS.name: Kansas
KS.scope: No statewide building code; cities and counties adopt and amend their own. State-owned buildings follow state agency requirements.
KS.citation: No state adoption found: Kansas has no statewide building code; cities and counties adopt under home rule
KS.draft_note: An absence has no adopting rule to cite. Read K.S.A. 31-134a: a building conforming to listed codes (incl. the 2000 IBC) is deemed to comply with the Kansas fire prevention code, and the State Fire Marshal specifies later editions by rule; this is a fire-code equivalency, not a building code. Secondary only: a 2012 AG opinion says K.A.R. 22-1-3(a) incorporated the 2006 IBC; AWC says the State Fire Marshal adopted the 2018 IBC and enforces building codes for state-owned buildings; a Dept. of Administration form (search snippet, link now 404) lists the 2018 IBC for state property. I could not read K.A.R. 22-1-3 (sos.ks.gov 403). If the signer confirms a state-buildings IBC, this could become 'limited' with that edition.
KS.icc_2026_10_20: Master I-Code chart (April 2026): IBC X (local adoptions only).

KY.name: Kentucky
KY.pending: DHBC KBC/KRC task forces are reviewing newer I-code editions (December 2025 notice, secondary); no rule filed.
KY.citation: 815 KAR 7:120 (Kentucky Building Code: 2015 IBC with the 2018 Kentucky Building Code amendments)
KY.draft_note: Read 815 KAR 7:120 on the LRC site: Section 2 makes the 2015 IBC the mandatory state building code for all buildings except 1-2 family and townhouses (815 KAR 7:125) and manufactured homes; the 2018 KBC amendments (Fourth Edition, February 2024) supersede where they conflict. History ends eff. 12-3-2024 (amendment-document update, not a new IBC edition). Read the DHBC 2018 KBC 4th ed.: a statewide uniform 'mini/maxi' code; Section 120.1 says plans submitted on or after August 1, 2019 shall conform, so 2019-08-01 is used. A 2018 KBC first edition (June 2018) on the same 2015 IBC base may have applied earlier (permitplace, secondary: eff. 8-22-2018, mandatory 2019-01-01); signer may prefer the earlier date. DHBC 'Find Currently Enforced Code' also lists the 2018 KBC based on the 2015 IBC.

LA.name: Louisiana
LA.pending: 2024 IBC proposed (notice of intent, La. Register 2026-08-20); the proposed rule says effective 2027-01-01. Final rule not seen.
LA.citation: LAC 17:I.103 (Louisiana State Uniform Construction Code; IBC 2021 Edition, excluding Chapters 1 and 27)
LA.draft_note: Read LAC 17 Part I (doa.la.gov .docx): 103.A adopts the 2021 IBC excluding Chapter 1 (Administration) and Chapter 27 (Electrical), with Louisiana amendments. Read the council's code information sheet: current IBC edition 2021; history table gives ICC codes effective dates; 2021 ICC codes effective 2023-01-01 (per IRC row reading of the same sheet, revised 2026-08-06); 'ICC code editions will become effective January 1, 2027' for the 2024 cycle. The 2024 adoption is a proposed rule (notice of intent 2026-08-20 per the IRC draft), so it is under 'pending', not 'upcoming'. Signer: check the Oct/Nov 2026 La. Register for a final rule.

ME.name: Maine
ME.scope: MUBEC applies statewide; enforcement is mandatory only in municipalities of 4,000+ residents, optional below that.
ME.citation: 16-642 C.M.R. ch. 3 (MUBEC Building Code; 2021 IBC, amended); ch. 1 sec. 6
ME.draft_note: Read 16-642 ch. 1 (MUBEC administration): sec. 6.1.A names the 2021 IBC with Maine amendments in ch. 3; sec. 4 says MUBEC applies to all buildings regardless of population, must be enforced at 4,000+ residents, and no municipality may enforce another building code. Read ch. 3: 'IBC' means the 2021 IBC; adopts listed chapters; effective 90 days after Commissioner approval; amended March 4, 2025 (filing 2025-044). The 2025-04-07 date is secondary (AIA Maine, Kennebunk, Brewer notices; Bar Harbor says Commissioner signed 2025-01-07); the State Fire Marshal MUBEC page that reportedly states it returned 403. Signer: confirm 2025-04-07 vs the 2025-03-04 filing date.

MD.name: Maryland
MD.pending: 2024 IBC proposed for COMAR 09.12.51 (Md. Register 2026-06-26, comments closed 2026-07-27); no final rule seen.
MD.scope: Statewide minimum (MBPS); counties and cities enforce it within 12 months of a state update and may adopt local amendments.
MD.citation: COMAR 09.12.51.04 (Maryland Building Performance Standards; 2021 IBC with State modifications)
MD.draft_note: Read the Department of Labor's COMAR 09.12.51 PDF: .04 incorporates the 2021 IBC (with .04B State modifications), 'Effective as of May 29, 2023'; .05 makes the IBC, IRC and IECC as modified the MBPS; .06B gives localities 12 months to implement (about 2024-05-29), so the edition at a given address can lag. The 2024 proposal is from search results (DOL building news); I did not read the Md. Register notice or find a final action.

MA.name: Massachusetts
MA.citation: 780 CMR 1.00-115.00 (Massachusetts State Building Code, 10th edition; 2021 IBC with MA amendments)
MA.draft_note: Read the mass.gov 10th edition handbook page via a 2026 Wayback copy (mass.gov blocks scripted access): the 10th edition 'became first effective on October 11, 2024' with a concurrency period (either 9th or 10th edition) extended to end 2025-06-30; it is based on modified 2021 I-codes, with 780 CMR 1.00-115.00 adopting the 35 chapters and appendices of the 2021 IBC, some replaced by MA chapters. The 9th edition (2015 IBC base) could still be used until 2025-06-30. I did not read 780 CMR itself. DOER stretch/specialized energy codes apply by municipality.

MI.name: Michigan
MI.citation: 2021 Michigan Building Code (LARA Bureau of Construction Codes; Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act)
MI.draft_note: LARA Code Books page read 2026-10-20: '2021 Michigan Building Code - Current Code - Effective April 9, 2025'; residential work is under the Michigan Residential Code (still 2015). The HBA v. LARA court pause concerns the 2021 residential rules, not the MBC. Admin Code rule number (R 408.30401 et seq.) and the prior MBC's effective date not read. The code is statewide; enforcement is by the local unit or, where it declines, the state Bureau.

MN.name: Minnesota
MN.pending: DLI is drafting a chapter 1305 update to the 2024 IBC (request for comments 2025-01-21); proposal, hearing and dates 'to be determined'.
MN.citation: Minn. R. 1305.0011 (Minnesota Building Code, 2018 IBC as amended); Minn. Stat. 326B.121
MN.draft_note: 1305.0011 subp. 1 read: 'the 2018 edition of the International Building Code' (history ends 44 SR 609). The page shows no effective date; 2020-03-31 is from DLI's 2020 building code fact sheet and the revisor's 'published electronically March 31, 2020' (fact sheet not re-read this pass). DLI 1305 docket read 2026-10-20: every step after the request for comments is 'To be determined'. As with the residential code, municipalities outside the metro area need not all enforce the code (opt-in by ordinance).

MS.name: Mississippi
MS.scope: Council codes are minimum codes; localities adopt one of the last 3 editions unless they opted out in 2014. Edition not confirmed.
MS.citation: Miss. Code Ann. 17-2-1 et seq., 17-2-4 (Mississippi Building Codes Council; State Uniform Construction Code), not read directly
MS.draft_note: SOURCES CONFLICT: ICC's April 2026 chart lists Mississippi IBC 24; BCAP and LegalClarity list the 2021 IBC effective 2024; AWC (updated March 2026) still lists the 2018 IBC (Council action December 2019). The Council's adopted-codes list and statute text could not be reached. Per a 2024 AG opinion paraphrasing 17-2-4: counties and cities must adopt one of the last three Council-adopted IBC/IRC editions unless they opted out within 120 days of 2014-08-01; coastal counties must enforce. MID modular rule (Title 19 Part 7 Ch. 3) uses the 2024 I-codes for modular homes from 2026-07-01. AWC says the Fire Prevention Code (2012 IBC) covers state-owned and some assembly/high-rise buildings. Kept 'local' with no edition, as the IRC row is, until the Council list is read; likely 'limited' after.
MS.icc_2026_10_20: Chart (April 2026): IBC 24 (state). State page: MBCC adopts on a 3-year cycle; coastal counties must enforce; voluntary elsewhere.

MO.name: Missouri
MO.scope: No statewide building code; cities and counties adopt their own edition.
MO.citation: No state adoption: Missouri has no statewide commercial building code; counties and cities adopt codes by ordinance
MO.draft_note: An absence has no adopting rule to cite; no Missouri statute was read. ICC's chart marks IBC X (local only). The state adopts a code for state-owned buildings (Office of Administration/FMDC), but its edition was not found: AWC pages variously say 2018 IBC (March 2026) and 2009 IBC (Dec 2023, Architecture Practice Act). If the signer wants a state-buildings row, read the FMDC design criteria first.
MO.icc_2026_10_20: Chart (April 2026): IBC X (local adoption only). State page: most codes adopted locally; state adopts for state-owned buildings.

MT.name: Montana
MT.citation: Admin. R. Mont. 24.301.131 (IBC 2024 as amended by ARM Title 24, Ch. 301)
MT.draft_note: DLI Current Codes page read 2026-10-20: 'International Building Code, 2024 Edition - Effective: September 26, 2026', amended by ARM Title 24 Ch. 301. Prior: 2021 IBC, effective 2022-06-11 (date carried from the IRC row's reading of the same page cache; not re-read). Justia's copy of ARM 24.301.131 (through Sept 2024) still shows 2021; the rule number is from that copy, the new rule text was not read. Certified city/county programs enforce the state code locally; the state enforces elsewhere.

NE.name: Nebraska
NE.scope: Applies where a county, city or village has not adopted a conforming code within 2 years of an update.
NE.draft_note: 71-6403(1)(a) read 2026-10-20: 'The International Building Code (IBC), 2018 edition' (from LB348, 2019; history to LB131, 2021). The 2019-09-07 date is ICC's, carried as in the IRC row; LB348 has no emergency clause and the operative date from the 2019 sine die (2019-05-31) was not confirmed from a primary source (MELT says 2019-09-01). LB164 (2023) proposed IBC 2021 Ch. 13 only; the current statute still names 2018. Local codes must conform generally (71-6406); failing that, the state code applies.

NV.name: Nevada
NV.scope: State code covers state buildings only (State Public Works Board); cities and counties adopt their own edition for other buildings.
NV.citation: NAC 341.045(1)(a) (State Public Works Board: 2024 IBC for state buildings), as amended by R072-24A
NV.draft_note: SPWD Adopted Codes list (rev. 2024-02-13) read: '2024 International Building Code (IBC)' under NAC 341.045; 2018-edition designs accepted until 2025-06-30. Cornell's NAC 341.045 copy names the 2024 IBC with history 'A by R072-24A, eff. 11/15/2024'; the leg.state.nv.us NAC page still shows the 2018 IBC (stale). Private buildings: local codes only (southern and northern Nevada regional amendments). The IRC row for NV is 'local'; this IBC row is 'limited' per the IBC brief's state-buildings rule.
NV.icc_2026_10_20: Chart (April 2026): IBC X (local only). State page: state adopts for state buildings; codes adopted locally.

NH.name: New Hampshire
NH.citation: RSA 155-A:1, IV (state building code: IBC 2024 with NH amendments), as amended 2026, eff. July 1, 2026
NH.draft_note: RSA 155-A:1, IV read 2026-10-20: adopts 'the International Building Code 2024' with board amendments approved as of 2025-10-10; source line ends 2026 ch. 49:1 and 318:3, eff. July 1, 2026. Prior: IBC 2021, effective 2024-07-01 (per the IRC row's history reading; not re-read). Town notices for the IRC say either edition may be used through 2026-12-31; whether that applies to the IBC was not read in the statute. Where a town has no building official, the State Fire Marshal enforces (155-A:2).

NJ.name: New Jersey
NJ.citation: N.J.A.C. 5:23-3.14 (building subcode: IBC/2024, New Jersey edition), R.2026 d.086
NJ.draft_note: Adoption notice 58 N.J.R. 8(2) read: amends 5:23-3.14 (building subcode) and the other subcodes for the 2024 model codes; adopted 2026-07-15, effective August 17, 2026. The notice's 3.14 text shows '(a) (No change.)', so the edition line itself was not seen; the 2024 adoption is stated throughout the responses. Six-month grace period (N.J.A.C. 5:23-1.6, not read): prior IBC/2021 usable until about 2027-02-17 (ICC-NTA). Prior: IBC/2021. The UCC is uniform statewide; localities may not amend.

NM.name: New Mexico
NM.citation: 14.7.2 NMAC (2021 New Mexico Commercial Building Code, adopting the 2021 IBC as amended)
NM.draft_note: 14.7.2.5 read: 'EFFECTIVE DATE: July, 14, 2023'; 14.7.2.8: 'adopts by reference the 2021 International Building Code, as amended'. History: 2015 NMCBC effective 2016-11-15 replaced by 2021 NMCBC effective 2023-07-14. No 2024 IBC rulemaking found. ICC says a few home-rule jurisdictions adopt their own codes.

NY.name: New York
NY.scope: Statewide outside New York City, which enforces its own NYC Construction Codes.
NY.citation: 19 NYCRR Part 1221 (2025 Building Code of New York State, Uniform Code)
NY.draft_note: DOS notice of adoption: 2025 Uniform Code incl. 2025 BCNYS effective 2025-12-31 (amended notice 2025-12-05 kept the date); permits filed on/after that date must comply; 2020 or 2025 optional before it. DOS Code Outreach 2026-1 (2026-02-03): NYS books 'based on the 2024 International Code Council books with New York modifications', and 19 NYCRR text also amends the books. 19 NYCRR 1221.1 PDF read (definitions only). A town notice says 2026-01-01; DOS says 2025-12-31. Fossil-fuel ban (1240.6, Subpart 1229-2) suspended by court order. Prior: 2020 BCNYS (2018 IBC). NYC excluded from the Uniform Code (own NYC Construction Codes).

NC.name: North Carolina
NC.pending: 2024 NC Building Code (2021 IBC) adopted; takes effect 12 months after OSFM certification under S.L. 2025-2; not yet certified.
NC.citation: N.C.G.S. 143-138; 2018 North Carolina State Building Code: Building Code (Office of State Fire Marshal)

OSFM Codes Current and Past: 2018 NC Codes effective 2019-01-01 'along with the 2015 International Codes'; accessibility row: '2018 North Carolina Building Code (based on the 2015 IBC)'. OSFM letter 2025-03-31 (read): S.L. 2025-2 sec. 5.12(b) makes all ten 2024 codes effective 12 months after the State Fire Marshal certifies publication/distribution AND a fully constituted Residential Code Council; until then the 2018 code governs; 2024 code usable as an alternate method on owner request (2018 Admin Code 102.5). Found no certification letter as of 2026-10-20. 2024 NCBC base = 2021 IBC per ICC/UpCodes (OSFM page does not name it).
NC.icc_2026_10_20: ICC chart (Apr 2026): IBC 21 (counts the adopted, not-yet-effective 2024 NCBC)

ND.name: North Dakota
ND.scope: Applies only where a city, county or township elects to enforce a building code; the state does not enforce it.
ND.citation: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-21.3 (North Dakota State Building Code), Dept. of Commerce, Division of Community Services
ND.draft_note: Commerce page: State Building Code updated to the 2024 IBC/IRC/IMC/IFGC, effective 2026-01-01; Commerce is 'not involved in the enforcement'. Read NDCC 54-21.3 (ndlegis.gov PDF): 54-21.3-03 code must consist of the international building, residential, mechanical and fuel gas codes; 54-21.3-05 a city/township/county may administer and enforce it. Exempt: state electrical, plumbing, fire codes (54-21.3-04). NDAC rule text adopting the 2024 edition not read. Home-rule cities may differ.

OH.name: Ohio
OH.citation: Ohio Adm. Code 4101:1-1-01 (2024 Ohio Building Code), Board of Building Standards
OH.draft_note: BBS Memo 2024-01-30 (read via Richland County copy): effective 2024-03-01 the OBC, OMC, OPC are 'based upon the 2021 International model codes'; applications filed on/after that date use the new codes; earlier filings stay on the 2017 OBC. codes.ohio.gov shows 4101:1-1-01 last effective 2025-10-15 (an amendment; text not shown there); Cornell LII copy of the rule, sec. 101.1, adopts 'International Building Code 2021 edition, Chapters 2 through 35 and appendix H'. The 2025-10-15 change appears to keep the 2021 base (not confirmed what it changed). Statewide for non-residential buildings, enforced by certified local departments or the state.

OK.name: Oklahoma
OK.citation: OAC 748:20-2-1 to -40 (OUBCC adoption of IBC 2024), 43 Ok Reg No. 20; 59 O.S. 1000.23
OK.draft_note: ICC chart lag, not a conflict: ICC Apr 2026 chart shows IBC 18 (predates the 2026-09-14 effective date). Read the OUBCC permanent rule PDF: 748:20-2-1 adopts IBC 2024 first printing (Aug 2023), amended, as the statewide minimum code for commercial construction, 'Amended at 43 Ok Reg, Number 20, effective 9-14-26'; OUBCC expressly did not adopt IBC 2021. No appendices adopted (locals may, 59 O.S. 1000.29). Prior: IBC 2018 eff 2021-09-14 (38 Ok Reg 2573). OUBCC web copy is unofficial; official text is the OAC/Ok Register (not read).

OR.name: Oregon
OR.citation: 2025 Oregon Structural Specialty Code (OAR ch. 918, div. 460), Building Codes Division
OR.draft_note: BCD commercial structures page: 2025 OSSC based on the 2024 IBC (plus 2024 IFC new-construction and 2024 IEBC); Chapter 1 effective and mandatory 2025-10-01; construction provisions effective 2025-10-01 with six-month phase-in (2022 OSSC or 2025 OSSC), mandatory 2026-04-01. Codebook history page agrees (2022 OSSC/2021 IBC eff 2022-10-01 to 2026-04-01). OAR number (918-460-0010) from general knowledge, not read. Adds Appendix Q (local single-exit path).

PA.name: Pennsylvania
PA.citation: 34 Pa. Code 403.21(a)(1) (Uniform Construction Code), amended 55 Pa.B. 7701
PA.draft_note: Read 34 Pa. Code 403.21: (a)(1) adopts Chapters 2-10, 12-29, 31-35 of the 'International Building Code of 2021' with exceptions; keeps 2015 IBC 704.2 and 704.4.1 and 2018 IBC 426.1. History: amended 2025-11-07, effective 2026-01-01, 55 Pa.B. 7701. Pre-2026 design contracts may use the 2018 UCC for a transition period (see IRC row). Prior: 2018 IBC. UCC applies statewide; L&I enforces commercial work in municipalities that opted out.

RI.name: Rhode Island
RI.draft_note: RI SOS rule page: adopts the 2021 IBC (later editions excluded); current version a 2025-12-01 technical revision (formatting), with an amendment effective 2025-12-01; prior version 2022-02-01 to 2025-12-01 (believed 2018 IBC per search results, that text not read). State/town notices (search only): 2021 codes effective 2025-12-01 with a 3-month prior-code grace, ended 2026-03-01. ICC chart shows IBC 21. No pending rulemaking listed.

SC.name: South Carolina
SC.citation: S.C. Code 6-9-50; LLR Building Codes Council adoption of the 2021 South Carolina Building Codes
SC.draft_note: LLR page: 2021 SC Building Codes adopted 2021-10-06, effective 2023-01-01 (page does not name the IBC; 2021 IBC per York County notice and ICC). Read LLR 2024 Final Modification Index PDF: Council adopted the 2024 IBC with SC modifications on 2025-08-26, implementation for local jurisdictions 2027-01-01; mandatory for all municipalities and counties under 6-9-50. Caveat: S.1078 (approves Reg. Doc. 5424, the IBC modifications) is still in Senate LC&I committee per scstatehouse.gov (as of 2026-04-17), so the SC modifications may not be final by 2027-01-01.

SD.name: South Dakota
SD.scope: Statewide design standard for non-residential buildings; locals may adopt and amend it; no state plan review or inspection.
SD.citation: SDCL 11-10-5 and 11-10-6 (2024 IBC), as amended by SL 2026, ch 59, 1-2
SD.draft_note: ICC chart lag, not a conflict: ICC Apr 2026 chart shows IBC 21; state law since SL 2026 ch 59 names the 2024 IBC (was 2021 under SL 2022 ch 35). Read via legislature API: 11-10-5 any local non-residential building ordinance must comply with the 2024 IBC (locals may amend/delete any portion); 11-10-6 where no local ordinance, the design standard for buildings commenced after 2026-07-01 must be based on the 2024 IBC (excludes residential, manufactured homes, farmsteads). No state enforcement; the 2026-07-01 date is from 11-10-6 text. Status 'statewide' is a design standard only; signer may prefer 'limited'.

TN.name: Tennessee
TN.scope: State minimum code; local governments that adopt and enforce their own codes under T.C.A. 68-120-101 may be exempt.
TN.citation: Tenn. Comp. R. & Regs. 0780-02-02-.01 (State Fire Marshal minimum codes: 2021 IBC with state amendments)
TN.draft_note: Read the SFMO 'Currently Adopted Codes' page (updated 2025-04-17): 'International Building Code (IBC), 2021 edition ... See Appendix for amendments'; history table row 4/17/2025 = IBC 2021. SFMO Codes Enforcement page: rule filing 01-17-25 effective April 17, 2025; plans needing SFMO approval could use the prior (2012) codes for 120 days, to 2025-08-15 (rule 0780-02-03-.11). Appendix amendments include ASCE 7-22 mapped Ss/S1 allowed, 2024 IBC flammable-gas provisions, classroom-door locking. Prior state IBC was 2012 (eff 2016-08-04). Note: Cornell LII's copy of 0780-02-02-.01 still shows the 2012 text (stale mirror; its history ends 2023), not treated as a conflict. Local governments meeting T.C.A. 68-120-101 may be exempt and enforce their own code; that statute and the exempt-jurisdiction list were not read. The 01-17-25 rule PDF itself was not read (tn.gov blocks automated fetches intermittently).

TX.name: Texas
TX.scope: Municipal commercial building code only (inside cities); cities may adopt later editions and local amendments. No county code.
TX.citation: Tex. Local Gov't Code 214.216 (IBC as it existed May 1, 2012, municipal commercial building code)
TX.draft_note: Read enrolled HB 738 (87R) Section 2: amends 214.216(a) from the May 1, 2003 IBC to the May 1, 2012 IBC, applies to all commercial buildings in a municipality; Section 5/6: applies to construction under agreements made on/after 2022-01-01; Act effective 2022-01-01. 214.216(d) lets cities adopt later ICC amendments and (e) keeps more stringent local codes, so most large cities enforce 2018/2021/2024. No statewide code outside municipalities (counties have no general building code authority). HB 871 (89R, 2025) would have moved the date to 2018/2021; per the IRC draft it passed the House and died in the Senate (not re-checked here). statutes.capitol.texas.gov is a JS app and was not read; codified text seen on texas.public.law (secondary).

UT.name: Utah
UT.citation: Utah Code 15A-2-103(1)(a) (State Construction Code: 2024 IBC incl. App. C and J), amended by Title 15A Ch. 3-4
UT.draft_note: Read current 15A-2-103 (Effective 7/1/2026): '(a) the 2024 edition of the International Building Code, including Appendices C and J'; the version effective 2027-01-01 keeps the 2024 IBC. Read enrolled H.B. 65 (2026 GS, Construction Code Amendments): line 71 '[2021] 2024 edition of the International Building Code'; Section 29 'this bill takes effect July 1, 2026'. Prior: 2021 IBC under HB 532 (2023), effective 2023-07-01 (le.utah.gov printout of the 2024-07-01 version still lists 2021). ICC's April 2026 chart shows 21, which predates the 2026-07-01 change (not a conflict). Uniform statewide code; statewide amendments 15A Ch. 3, local amendments Ch. 4.
UT.icc_2026_10_20: IBC 21 (ICC chart, April 2026; predates the 2026-07-01 move to 2024)

VT.name: Vermont
VT.scope: Applies to 'public buildings' (commercial, multifamily, rentals); owner-occupied single-family homes are excluded.
VT.citation: Vermont Fire & Building Safety Code 2025 (Div. of Fire Safety rule; adopts 2021 IBC/IEBC), under 20 V.S.A. ch. 173
VT.draft_note: Read the 2025 VT Fire & Building Safety Code PDF: cover 'EFFECTIVE DATE: 11/04/2025'; adopted codes NFPA 101 2021, NFPA 1 2021, 'INTERNATIONAL BUILDING CODE - IBC - 2021', IEBC 2021; Section 5 amends the 2021 IBC; Section 12(1) 'These rules shall take effect 11/04/2025'; 12(2) projects permitted and started under the 2015 code within 180 days may continue. Where NFPA 101 or NFPA 1 conflicts with the IBC, those NFPA codes govern. Applies to 'public buildings' (20 V.S.A. 2730), which excludes owner-occupied single-family homes and farm buildings; the DFS codes page lists the prior 2015 code as 10/10/16-11/05/25 (one-day mismatch with 11/04/2025). Prior IBC 2015.

VA.name: Virginia

Uniform statewide; localities may not amend. 2024 cycle: NOIRA 2025-03-10, BHCD considered proposals 2026-05-11; DHCD slides (secondary) projected 2024 Virginia codes effective Oct 2027, but no proposed or final regulation was found.

WV.name: West Virginia

WI.name: Wisconsin

WI.draft_note: Read SPS 361.05(1): 'The International Building Code - 2021, subject to the modifications specified in chs. SPS 361 to 366 is incorporated by reference'; history 'CR 23-007: am. Register August 2025 No. 836, eff. 9-1-25'. Prior: 2015 IBC (CR 16-094, eff. 2018-05-01). SPS 361.02: applies to all public buildings and places of employment (incl. multifamily); 1-2 family dwellings are under the Uniform Dwelling Code instead. Uniform statewide code. Any transition/plan-submittal grace period for CR 23-007 not checked.

WY.name: Wyoming
WY.scope: State code via fire marshal plan review for public, school, assembly, multi-story and >5,000 sq ft buildings; local codes elsewhere.
WY.citation: 041-1 Wyo. Code R. 1-2(a)(i) (Council on Fire Prevention and Electrical Safety: 2024 IBC), W.S. 35-9-108 plan review
WY.draft_note: Read rule 041-1 Wyo. Code R. 1-2 on Cornell LII (mirror): '(i) The International Building Code, 2024 Edition'; note 'Amended, Eff. 6/26/2024'. Read the State Fire Marshal plan-review page: 'The State of Wyoming, on June 28, 2024 adopted the 2024 International Codes'; new submissions from June 28, 2024 must comply (2-day mismatch with the rule's 6/26/2024 effective date; used the rule date). State plan review (W.S. 35-9-108) covers state/local government buildings, schools, buildings over 5,000 sq ft with public access, multi-story buildings, assembly, child care >10, and remodels >= $40,000. No general statewide building code; cities/counties adopt their own. Delegation to local jurisdictions (W.S. 35-9-121) not read.
